entries.summary: Documented ES SigV4 signing estate: upgraded modules still on v1 for ES; acm19 3.0.0 is v2 + HttpClient4/5; Jest/RHLC both EOL
entries.detail: ES SigV4 signing analysis added as section 10 of 2026-08-19-lambda-aws-refactor.md. Key findings: (1) The 'AWS-upgraded/COMPLETED' service modules STILL sign Elasticsearch with AWS SDK v1 - visibility uses com.amazonaws.auth.AWS4Signer + DefaultAWSCredentialsProviderChain + a copied-in-repo awslabs interceptor clone (visibility-inbound/config/ElasticSearchClientModule.java + inbound/aws/AwsRequestSigner.java) around RestHighLevelClient; ES signing is the common v1 holdout because cloud-sdk has no ES signing abstraction. (2) booking (IN PROGRESS) and webbl (COMPLETED) use Jest (io.searchbox.JestClient) but only @Inject it - no JestClient is built anywhere in this repo, so it comes from the shared commons library; their signing is a commons concern. (3) acm19 3.0.0 (verified in ~/.m2): signs with AWS SDK v2 (software.amazon.awssdk:auth:2.27.17), ships AwsRequestSigningApacheInterceptor (HttpClient 4.x) + AwsRequestSigningApacheV5Interceptor (5.x), both httpclient 4.5.14 and httpclient5 5.3.1 as provided; it is the community successor to archived amazon-archives interceptor, healthy cadence but no active maintainers. (4) Premise 'Jest only works with v1 signing' is false - Apache interceptor decouples signer from client, so v2 signer works with Jest (oceanschedules-process already injects an interceptor into Jest, just v1). (5) Both ES clients are EOL: RestHighLevelClient deprecated 7.15/removed 8.0 (6.6.2 is 2019), Jest abandoned ~2019. Option A removes v1 SDK but keeps EOL client; durable end-state is opensearch-java + AwsSdk2Transport (Option B).

entries.summary: Confirmed v1 Jest+signing (vc.inreach 0.0.22 + aws-java-sdk-core + Jest) shaded in booking/tx-tracking; acm19 unused anywhere; AWS upgrade never migrated ES signing
entries.detail: CORRECTION + evidence (updated section 10 of 2026-08-19-lambda-aws-refactor.md). User was right: booking/tx-tracking/webbl DO carry v1 Jest+signing deps. OWASP dependency-check reports (owasp-reports/booking, owasp-reports/tx-tracking, built 2026-08-16) prove the shaded uber-jars bundle: com.amazonaws:aws-java-sdk-core:1.12.730 (+ s3/sns/sqs/kms/ses v1), io.searchbox:jest:5.3.3 + jest-common, and vc.inreach.aws:aws-signing-request-interceptor:0.0.22 (the actual v1 SigV4 signer for Jest; MIT ~2016, abandoned). So even 'COMPLETED' modules (tx-tracking, webbl) still ship AWS SDK v1 for ES signing. Three distinct v1 signing mechanisms in the estate: (a) vc.inreach.aws AWSSigner/AWSSigningRequestInterceptor for Jest (booking/tx-tracking/webbl/oceanschedules-process); (b) copied-in-repo awslabs clone AwsRequestSigner + AWS4Signer for visibility (RHLC); (c) external awslabs jitpack interceptor + AWS4Signer for elasticsearch-purge lambda (RHLC). NO module uses acm19 - repo grep for acm19/io.github.acm19 = zero hits; acm19 is only the proposed Option A. Git provenance: visibility AwsRequestSigner written by pbono 2021-07-19 ('Avoided dependency by writing aws interceptor signer', pre-upgrade, v1); visibility ElasticSearchClientModule last touched by Arijit Kundu 2026-06-23 under ION-12316 (visibility AWS SDK 2.x) but that commit was rebase/conflict/test-fix and LEFT signing on v1; elasticsearch-purge Processor by sgo001 2020, updated Mukesh Vellanki 2025 (ION-11880 JDK17), never migrated. So the AWS 2.x upgrade did NOT migrate ES signing off v1 in any module.

entries.summary: Aligned ES-signing doc: added Direct-Answers TL;DR, corrected booking->COMPLETED, clarified 'clone', refined acm19/Option A stance and tables
entries.detail: Aligned/consistency-fixed section 9-10 of 2026-08-19-lambda-aws-refactor.md per review: (1) Added section 10.0 'Direct answers' TL;DR answering: all ES modules sign with v1 today (Jest via vc.inreach 0.0.22, RHLC via AWS4Signer+awslabs); v1 signing is valid-but-not-required with Jest; v2 signing CAN be used with existing Jest (acm19 HttpClient-4.x interceptor swapped into JestClientFactory); the visibility 'in-repo clone' = hand-copied source of archived awslabs AWSRequestSigningApacheInterceptor (still v1); acm19 makes sense only as short bridge (esp for the lambda where it fully de-v1s) since it's used nowhere and keeps EOL clients - opensearch-java+AwsSdk2Transport is the strategic fix. (2) Corrected booking status IN PROGRESS -> COMPLETED throughout. (3) Clarified 'clone' wording. (4) Refined Option A framing: clean full de-v1 win for elasticsearch-purge lambda, only partial de-v1 (bridge) for service modules which shade other v1 aws-java-sdk jars. entries.summary: Validated Jest-v2-signing constraint via javap: not a runtime impossibility; real blocker is hard-typed commons JestClientBuilder API + additive-only rule + X-G8 decision to prefer OpenSearch SDK
entries.detail: Validated the 'JestClient cannot use v2 signing' constraint against actual class signatures (javap) rather than just the commons doc claim; documented as section 11 of 2026-08-19-lambda-aws-refactor.md. SOURCE: booking/tx-tracking/webbl get their signed JestClient from mercury-services-commons cloud-sdk-aws/.../aws/module/JestModule.java (newAwsSigningClient) which uses vc.inreach.aws.AWSSigner over v1 DefaultAWSCredentialsProviderChain; the cloud-sdk-api/commons JestClientBuilder constructor is HARD-TYPED to concrete vc.inreach.aws.request.AWSSigningRequestInterceptor. AUTHORITATIVE DECISION: cloud-sdk-api/docs/2026-07-23-sdk-gap-appway-aws-upgrade-design.md section 7.1 gap X-G8 says the earlier 'v2 interceptor' note was WRONG, booking/visibility/webbl Jest usage is 'compatible with the vc.inreach 1.x signer only', ES signing is orthogonal to the v1->v2 flip, and OpenSearch-SDK is a separate future workstream. TECHNICAL VALIDATION (javap on both m2 jars): BOTH vc.inreach AWSSigningRequestInterceptor:0.0.22 and acm19 AwsRequestSigningApacheInterceptor:3.0.0 implement the SAME org.apache.http.HttpRequestInterceptor with the SAME process(HttpRequest,HttpContext), and BOTH buffer the request body (vc.inreach body()->Optional<byte[]>/TO_BYTE_ARRAY; acm19 lambda$process$0(ByteArrayOutputStream)->InputStream). acm19 constructor takes v2 types (HttpSigner<AwsCredentialsIdentity>, AwsCredentialsProvider, Region). CONCLUSION: NO fundamental runtime impossibility - Jest CAN be signed with v2 (acm19 4.x interceptor is a drop-in at the Apache HttpClient 4.x layer). The REAL blocker is the hard-typed shared commons JestClientBuilder API (widening it to the HttpRequestInterceptor interface is a breaking, non-additive change the appianway program forbids) + no v2 port of vc.inreach + strategic decision to retire Jest via OpenSearch SDK. Corrected my earlier overstated 'v2 works with Jest as a simple drop-in' answer.

entries.summary: Fixed Sonar new-code coverage on registration-archive & auth-tokens-archive HandlerSupport/Processor; amended + force-pushed
entries.detail: Fixed additional Sonar 'Coverage on New Code' gate failures on two more lambda modules (integration tests do not count toward Sonar; only unit tests do). registration-archive: HandlerSupport.java was 0% (16 lines) and Processor.java 44.2% (25 lines/18 conditions). auth-tokens-archive: HandlerSupport.java 47.4% (10 lines). Root cause: per-module HandlerSupport client factories (newS3Client/newDynamoDbClient/createStorageClient/createNotificationService) and resolveRegion/resolveCredentialsProvider seams had no UNIT tests, and Processor.toPlainValue's number/bool/map/list/string-set/number-set/null branches were only hit by the IT. Fixes: (1) new registration HandlerSupportClientUnitTest (10 tests) covering resolveRegion(Supplier) 3 branches, resolveRegion() no-arg, resolveCredentialsProvider, newS3Client/newDynamoDbClient via Mockito.mockStatic on the cloud-sdk factories (CI-safe, no AWS creds), plus getTableName/getAWSRegion/getS3BucketName throw-path; (2) registration ProcessorUnitTest new all-attribute-types test to cover toPlainValue branches; (3) auth-tokens HandlerSupportUnitTest extended (4->7) with createStorageClient/createNotificationService via mockStatic + no-arg resolveRegion. Local JaCoCo now: registration Processor 93.8% line (branch 39/40), registration HandlerSupport 84% line + 4/4 branch (~86% Sonar-combined), auth-tokens HandlerSupport 100%. Full verify green incl. DynamoDB-Local ProcessorIT. Note: getTableName-style one-line getters can't be line-covered via the throwing path (JaCoCo exit-probe doesn't fire on exception); success-path would need junit-pioneer @SetEnvironmentVariable, not added to registration (margin already sufficient). JsonSupport.java (57%) and Utils.java overall (73.8%) are NOT new code in this commit so Sonar does not gate them. Amended into single ION-16415 commit (6925e289b9, 42 files) and force-pushed with --force-with-lease. PR #1194.
